report.title: Base16 length calculations and formatting-error conversion
report.explanation: For base16ct 1.0.0, decoded_len terminates normally for every input slice. It returns Ok of exactly half the input length when that length is even, and Err(InvalidLength) exactly when it is odd. It examines length only, so this result does not validate hexadecimal characters. encoded_len returns exactly twice the input length without a panic when the length is at most usize::MAX / 2. The handwritten From<Error> conversion into core::fmt::Error always returns the formatting error value normally for either source error, intentionally discarding which error occurred. These are body proofs of the unchanged published APIs; the length proofs quantify arbitrary slice lengths representable in the model.

report.limitations: Only decoded_len, encoded_len and From<Error> for core::fmt::Error are covered; Display formatting is not proved. Hexadecimal encoding, decoding, character validation, destination writes, allocation and encode_str's unchecked UTF-8 conversion are not verified. encoded_len behavior above usize::MAX / 2 is outside the proved precondition. Other targets, feature configurations and release overflow behavior were not checked.

report.title: Exact PCG state, output and advance for all four generator types
report.explanation: For rand_pcg 0.10.2, the four state getters return their stored word. The three LCG stream getters return increment>>1; from_state preserves its input state and stores increment=(stream<<1) OR 1, discarding the highest stream bit. Their new constructors initialize state=((input_state+increment)*multiplier+increment) with modular arithmetic; the multipliers are 6364136223846793005, 47026247687942121848144207491837523525 and 15750249268501108917 respectively. Mcg128Xsl64::new stores input_state OR 1. Native output proofs retain Lcg64Xsh32::try_next_u32 and both word widths for the three 128-bit types. The XSL-RR variants permute the newly advanced state; CM-DXSM permutes the old state then advances. Their 32-bit methods return the low 32 bits of the 64-bit result with the same final state. Original Result::map and conversion closures are body-extracted. Mcg128Xsl64::advance additionally terminates normally for every u128 delta and every internal u128 state, returning state=M^delta*initial_state modulo 2^128, M=47026247687942121848144207491837523525. A well-founded halving-loop proof connects the original body to this ordinary power specification, covering all deltas without an artificial execution bound. These twenty-five direct original-body API guarantees apply under default and serde because the selected official translations are byte-identical; the serde implementations themselves remain unproved. Each of the three LCG advance methods also terminates normally for every full-width delta, state and increment, preserving the stored increment and producing exactly delta repetitions of the ordinary modular affine step x↦M*x+increment. An independent linear recurrence specifies this behavior; a generic affine-composition proof connects the original binary algorithm to it. Increments need not be odd for this state-transform identity. Separate Kani evidence calls the unchanged Mcg128Xsl64::from_seed and public state getter for every sixteen-byte seed. Its state equals the independently decoded little-endian u128 seed OR 1 (242 successful checks under each of default and serde). The exact rand_core 0.10.0 and serde 1.0.228 dependency lock is retained. This is a separate Kani body guarantee, not another Aeneas machine claim or a formal cross-tool equivalence proof.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models, source adaptations or local trusted helper contracts are used. All twenty-one API theorem dependency audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Wrapping arithmetic, shifts, casts and rotations use official standard-library models, rather than proofs of Rust std implementation bodies. The original Result::map body is extracted and proved through its actual closure calls, rather than supplied by a custom model.
report.limitations: Coverage is the twenty-five named bodies on x86_64 under default or serde. Internal word states include zero/even values that usual seed constructors may not produce, but all are valid Rust scalar data; no seed-reachability claim is made. Stream getter behavior for arbitrary increments is proved, but no save/restore identity is claimed for an arbitrary even increment. Aeneas byte-seed/from_seed/seed_from_u64 contracts, Lcg64Xsh32::try_next_u64, buffer filling, RNG callbacks/forking, manual Debug, serde and inherited/external blanket APIs remain outside these Aeneas claims. No period, jump-back interpretation for wrapped negative strides, statistical quality or cryptographic security is established. Other targets and dependency feature combinations were not checked.

report.title: Exact next-word updates and separately checked seed/nonzero properties
report.explanation: For rand_xorshift 0.5.0, the Aeneas proof establishes the exact try_next_u32 word and state update for every four-u32 state, using three explicit std wrapping-operator models. With t=x XOR (x << 11), r=w XOR (w >> 19) XOR t XOR (t >> 8); the returned value is Ok(r) and state becomes (y,z,w,r), using 32-bit logical operations. A separate Lean theorem derives preservation of a nonzero state from this exact transition. Independently, Kani checks the unchanged from_seed body for every 16-byte seed: four little-endian u32 words are decoded, and the all-zero input is replaced by four 0x0BAD5EED words. The constructed state is nonzero. A second Kani harness checks that the original next_u32 body preserves every nonzero four-word state. These seed and preservation checks are supplementary Kani results, not an Aeneas seed-body claim. No original Rust source or manifest is changed.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, Charon/Aeneas translation, existing Aeneas scalar primitives, Lean kernel, and Kani/CBMC toolchains are trusted. Three executable std Wrapping<u32> models connect shift-left, shift-right, and xor to existing Aeneas primitives. Kani checks their Rust correspondence for all u32 operands and all 64-bit usize shift amounts; the relation between these Rust formulas and the Lean definitions remains an explicitly reviewed semantic bridge, not an in-Lean proof of the std bodies. No extra local axiom occurs in the public theorem's transitive dependencies. The seed and preservation harnesses embed the entire original Rust implementation as an unchanged prefix, appending safe observers in a std verification module. This preserves the implementation text but retains the documented verification-module and compiler/toolchain boundary. The separate Nonzero.lean proof uses the existing Aeneas exact transition theorem, not an assumed new seed theorem.
report.limitations: The single Aeneas API mapping remains try_next_u32 on x86_64 without serde. from_seed and original nonzero-state preservation are independent Kani body checks. Kani uses Rust nightly-2026-08-21 while Aeneas extraction uses nightly-2026-09-17; these are not mechanically linked proofs of one toolchain's std bodies. The all-zero state is still covered by the exact step theorem; the initial-nonzero guarantee is for from_seed, not every unverified initialization or serialization path. next_u64, fill_bytes, external-RNG initialization, formatting, inherited Rng wrappers and serde remain unverified. report.title: Exact xoshiro word outputs, projections and Seed512 byte views
report.explanation: For rand_xoshiro 0.8.1, the unchanged native word-generating method of each of its fifteen generators returns Ok of the specified output scrambler and performs the exact documented word-state transition. Coverage includes SplitMix64, both xoroshiro64 variants, all three xoroshiro128 variants, and all three variants of each xoshiro128, xoshiro256 and xoshiro512 family. For 32-bit-word engines the native method is try_next_u32; for 64-bit-word engines it is try_next_u64. SplitMix64::try_next_u32 is also proved independently, including its distinct Mix4 output formula, among the direct body proofs. Each theorem covers arbitrary internal words, including all-zero states, and establishes normal termination in the Aeneas model. Array-state representation theorems establish that the four-word and eight-word inputs cover every valid fixed-length engine state. Exact output formulas and resulting fields are defined independently of the generated Rust body in the output*/next* specifications. The selected original bodies have byte-identical official Aeneas translations under the default and serde feature configurations, so these body guarantees apply to both configurations; this does not verify the serde trait implementations. Nine further 32-bit APIs are verified through exact forwarding selectors whose calls to the unchanged original API are inlined by the Rust compiler: all three xoroshiro128, all three xoshiro256 and all three xoshiro512 variants. These establish the same state transition as their 64-bit method, with low 32 output bits for xoroshiro128++ and xoroshiro128**, and high 32 bits for the other seven variants. The selector source, typed receiver/return correspondence, target, original method inline scopes and absence of unknown externals are guarded. Default and serde selected programs are byte-identical. Four additional direct body proofs cover Seed512: Default initializes all 64 bytes to zero; AsRef exposes exactly the stored bytes; AsMut exposes those bytes and writes back every legal 64-byte replacement unchanged; iter initializes the standard slice-iterator model over those same bytes at position zero. SplitMix64::state is additionally proved to return exactly the eight little-endian bytes of its complete internal u64 state, for every state including zero. Thirty registered APIs comprise twenty-one direct bodies and nine compiler-inlined calls. Separate Kani evidence checks the five remaining 32-bit-engine try_next_u64 APIs against independent two-step little-endian word composition and exact poststate formulas for every internal state, including zero, under default and serde features. Each configuration passes five ordinary harnesses and 892 checks. These are separate Kani guarantees, not Aeneas machine claims or a cross-tool equivalence theorem.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas array/scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models, source adaptations or local helper axioms are used. All API and supplementary direct/selector theorems have dependency audits permitting only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Standard shifts, rotations, wrapping arithmetic and array operations use official Aeneas models, rather than body proofs of Rust std implementations. The nine selector proofs additionally rely on Rust compiler inlining of the exact original API call; retained MIR scopes identify each original TryRng method and Rng wrapper. The selector does not replace or assume an opaque original API: generated native callees are body-proved and no unknown external definitions remain. Seed512 byte-view and iterator initialization proofs use the official array-to-slice and slice-iterator models. The mutable reference model specifies write-back of the fixed-length referent; resizing that referent is not a legal returned-slice operation in safe Rust.
report.limitations: Only twenty-one direct bodies and nine compiler-inlined original-API forwarding calls are covered, with default or serde features on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. report.title: Exact integer writes and misuse checks in NoHashHasher
report.explanation: For nohash-hasher 0.2.0 on x86_64 with std enabled or disabled, Default initializes the stored value to zero, Clone preserves state, and finish returns the stored integer. Each of the ten integer write methods stores the Rust conversion of its input to u64: unsigned values are widened and signed values are converted modulo 2^64. With debug assertions enabled, the first integer write succeeds and a later write fails its assertion. With debug assertions disabled, each integer write replaces the stored value. The generic byte-slice write always panics in both configurations. These are exact per-method state and result contracts over all inputs, proved from unchanged published Rust bodies. Separate original-body Kani evidence checks handwritten Debug::fmt for NoHashHasher<u8> after Default or one arbitrary write_u8, using default {:?} formatting into a fixed 64-byte writer. Successful output has exact tuple delimiters, canonical decimal state and, in debug mode, the correct written flag. A writer that errors on its first call propagates Err and leaves its buffer unchanged. All std/no_std dependency and debug/release combinations pass separately: 2175 debug and 2143 release checks in each feature configuration; the verification harness itself uses std. This is a bounded formatter/input-domain supplement, not another Aeneas API claim or a proof for arbitrary stored u64 values, writers, formatting options or partial-write failures. A separate Kani supplement executes the actual standard Clone::clone_from default body and original manual Clone for NoHashHasher<u64>, in all four configurations. Source and destination independently begin at Default or one arbitrary write_u64. Public finish checks destination replacement and source preservation; a distinct full-original-prefix fixture with read-only getters also checks the debug written flag. The eight jobs succeed (public-value stage 47 debug or 28 release checks, flag-observer stage 104 or 81 checks per feature configuration). This concrete reachable-state Rust-body guarantee is separate from the generic Lean composition through the official default model; arbitrary T, other std revisions and other state histories remain unproved.

report.title: Exact integer generation, seed initialization and state restoration in Rand32 and Rand64
report.explanation: For oorandom 11.1.5, twelve unchanged APIs have exact value/state proofs: new, new_inc, state, from_state, the unsigned output method and the signed output method for both Rand32 and Rand64. For arbitrary seed and increment input, new_inc normalizes the stream to ((increment << 1) OR 1), starts at zero, performs one PCG state update, adds the seed modulo the state width, then performs a second PCG state update. new uses the published DEFAULT_INC. state returns the exact current state and increment, and from_state restores those values unchanged; two additional composition theorems establish save/restore identity. Unsigned generation returns the exact PCG-XSH-RR output permutation of the old state and advances to multiplier*state+increment modulo 2^64 or 2^128. Signed generation preserves that updated state and reinterprets the unsigned result bits as i32 or i64. Each covered call terminates normally in the Aeneas model for every scalar input, including zero states and even restored increments. Separate Kani harnesses directly check both original rand_float methods after restoring arbitrary complete state and increment, including zero states and even increments. Each returns an IEEE value greater than or equal to zero and strictly less than one (two harnesses, 33 checks each). This is a separate range-only body guarantee; exact float bits and poststate were not established, and no cross-tool equivalence or Aeneas machine claim is added.

report.title: Either branch operations and conditional callback composition
report.explanation: Twelve callback APIs compose a supplied mathematical callback contract with variant selection. is_left_and/right_and apply the callback only to the indicated variant and otherwise return false; is_left_or/right_or return true on the indicated variant and apply the callback to the other. map_left/right map only the named payload and preserve the other variant and payload. map_left_or/right_or return the mapped named payload or the supplied default. left_or_else/right_or_else preserve the named payload or compute it from the opposite payload. left_and_then/right_and_then return the selected callback-produced Either unchanged, or preserve the opposite variant and payload. Their normal-result proofs explicitly assume the supplied FnOnce dictionary returns the mathematical function value on every argument. Separate companion theorems show selected callback failure is propagated unchanged and non-selected branches preserve their result without any callback success premise. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the following value-semantic guarantees exclude payload destructor effects; they do not establish Rust panic freedom for arbitrary Drop implementations. In that model, is_left/is_right identify the actual branch; left/right return the corresponding optional payload; left_or/right_or select that payload or the given default; flip swaps the branch and a separate composition theorem proves flipping twice returns the original value. left_and/right_and select the supplied value or preserve the opposite payload. factor_none moves the optional payload outside Either while retaining its tag. factor_first/factor_second move the common tuple component outside Either. as_ref preserves the variant and referenced value; as_mut preserves the initial view and its generated backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back to the original variant. The twenty-six original bodies terminate normally in the model for all well-typed values in their stated domains.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are assumed; callback behavior is an explicit premise of the conditional composition theorems. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value and backward-function semantics; they do not independently verify the compiler borrow checker or Rust aliasing model.
report.limitations: Callback termination, panic freedom, captured-state effects and concrete closure correctness are not established by these conditional composition proofs. The theorem hypotheses describe modeled FnOnce results; unchanged modeled failure propagation does not specify Rust panic payloads, unwinding or external effects. Only the twenty-six named methods and the two-flip composition are proved. Other inherent and callback-taking APIs, iterators, pinning, standard trait implementations and serde remain unproved. Rust destructor behavior and resource consumption are outside the pure value model. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.

report.title: ASCII classification, string views and sequence updates
report.explanation: For ascii 1.1.0, as_byte returns the exact ASCII code for every valid AsciiChar. The eleven classification methods are correct for all 128 characters: digits are characters '0' through '9'; alphabetic is A-Z or a-z; alphanumeric additionally accepts digits; lowercase and uppercase accept a-z and A-Z respectively; hexdigit accepts 0-9, A-F or a-f. Graphic accepts byte codes 33-126 and printable accepts 32-126. Blank accepts space or tab; whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR and FF, rejecting vertical tab; control accepts codes 0-31 or 127. eq_ignore_ascii_case returns exactly whether the two codes are equal after mapping A-Z to a-z and leaving other codes unchanged; the independent mathematical equivalence is proved for all 128 squared valid pairs. For the AsciiChar implementation of ToAsciiChar, the checked method always returns Ok of the same value and the unchecked method returns that same value. is_ascii_punctuation accepts exactly ASCII intervals 33-47, 58-64, 91-96 and 123-126. The hand-written Default implementation returns the NUL enum value. AsAsciiStrError::valid_up_to returns its stored index; this does not establish that a separate validator found the first invalid byte. The public is_alphabetic, is_alphanumeric, is_lowercase and is_uppercase methods satisfy the same letter/digit predicates. is_whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR, VT and FF. For every u32 radix, is_digit returns normally at radix 0-36 and accepts exactly characters whose digit value (0-9 or case-independent A-Z values 10-35) is below the radix; other characters return false. Thus radix 0 always returns false and radix 1 accepts only character '0'. Every radix above 36 panics. The other twenty-three character/error bodies terminate normally in the model. AsciiStr::as_slice preserves the complete character sequence; as_mut_slice supplies that initial view and its generated backward function writes every valid same-length replacement back exactly. AsciiStr::len gives the exact sequence length and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. For an already valid AsciiStr receiver, the AsAsciiStr checked conversion returns Ok with the unchanged view, its unchecked conversion is the same view, and the AsMutAsciiStr unchecked conversion preserves the initial view and exact same-length valid replacement writeback. These original implementations are identities, not raw byte casts or validation of other input types. AsciiString::new produces an empty sequence, len returns its exact length, and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. push writes back the original sequence followed by the supplied character below the model length limit; at model length usizeMAX it fails with maximumSizeExceeded. Separately, Kani directly checked the original checked ToAsciiChar bodies for u8, i8, u16, u32 and char over their complete type domains: Ok exactly for ASCII-range inputs, preserving the codepoint, and Err otherwise. Those five body-check results are separate evidence and are not additional Lean API claims. Seven separate Kani checks also verify original case conversion and mutable writeback, as_char, case-insensitive equality and printable control pictures over all 128 valid characters (all pairs for equality). These establish A-Z/a-z mapping, exact receiver updates, ASCII code preservation and U+2400 control pictures with DEL at U+2421.
report.trusted_assumptions: Borrowed slice contracts use the generated value and backward-function semantics. They do not independently establish Rust pointer identity, lifetime or aliasing rules, and no resizing through a mutable slice is claimed. The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. Proofs split the complete finite AsciiChar type and use kernel-checked logical reduction and proved scalar arithmetic, without native-evaluation trust. The byte-code table contains each actual ASCII variant in code order. Transitive axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no custom models or local axioms are introduced. Separate Kani body checks trust Kani/CBMC, their standard/intrinsic semantics and their pinned Rust compiler; no mechanized cross-tool equivalence is claimed.
report.limitations: Thirty-five API mappings are Lean-proved; the other explicitly described scalar/case results are separate Kani body checks. The identity proofs for unsafe methods apply only to their original AsciiChar and AsciiStr receiver implementations, which perform no raw cast. They establish nothing about unchecked conversions from integers, char, byte slices, str or other trait implementations. The Lean mathematical code-fold is not a proof of the separate case-conversion APIs; those original bodies instead have the separately recorded full-domain Kani checks. General input validation, the remaining AsciiStr/AsciiString APIs, allocation, serde and arbitrary unsafe conversions remain unproved. The official Vec model stores only element sequences and a length bound. It does not represent capacity, Rust isizeMAX allocation limits, allocator availability, OS failure or OOM. Thus the push result and failure partition are properties of that model; no exact physical allocation/panic behavior or capacity preservation is claimed. Case conversion and printable-picture behavior have separate Kani evidence, not Lean proofs. Invalid enum representations are outside the input domain. The original is_digit_strange_radixes test fails on the pinned modern Rust because char::is_digit panics at radix 0/1; the crate is_digit API is covered separately for all radix values; the failed test comparison invokes std char::is_digit at radix 0/1. Remaining original tests pass with only that test excluded. The five checked scalar conversion bodies and the stated case/character bodies have separate Kani evidence, rather than additional Lean claims. The original AsciiChar::new constructor is checked only on ASCII inputs by the generator; its non-ASCII panic domain remains unproved. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.
